rows.evidence: Q1: Abstract <U+2013> the authors report their own qualitative data from interviews with 60 coffee farmers and experts in Dak Lak Province and a causal loop diagram they formulated from it.
rows.notes: Extended abstract only. The study is a qualitative system-dynamics causal loop analysis of drought impacts on coffee in Dak Lak; it identifies over-irrigation and groundwater exploitation as drivers of drought impacts and merely proposes 'promotion of technologies and policy measures on efficient water use for irrigation' as a management strategy. It does not test, measure or model drip or sensor-based irrigation, nor any effect of such technology on drought resilience; the quantitative simulation model is stated to be still in progress. The study thus supports at most the problem diagnosis (over-irrigation contributing to water scarcity) upstream of the claimed adaptation effect.

notes: Document is a one-page extended abstract (MODSIM 2019) with no methods detail, tables or figures; only a qualitative causal loop diagram based on literature and interviews is reported, and the simulation model is described as in progress.
